skill.name: canvas-design
skill.description: Create polished visual art as PNG or PDF files using an explicit design philosophy, minimal text, and bundled typography assets.
skill.summary: Create design-forward canvas artwork from a written visual philosophy.
skill.author: Cam10001110101

security_audit.summary: Most system reconnaissance and shell execution alerts are false positives from license text and Markdown. The skill still includes many unscanned binary font files and asks agents to download arbitrary fonts. I also found one prompt-injection style sentence that fabricates prior user context.

remediation.issue: Bundled binary fonts lack marketplace-visible provenance.
remediation.suggestion: Document source URLs and hashes for each font, and replace any file that fails trusted font validation.

remediation.issue: The skill allows open-ended external font downloads.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the open-ended download sentence and require bundled fonts or approved sources only.

remediation.issue: The instructions fabricate a prior user request.
remediation.suggestion: Rewrite the statement as a quality guideline without claiming the user already requested it.

content.value_statement: Static visual projects can drift into generic layouts or text-heavy documents. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to build a design philosophy, then express it as polished PNG or PDF artwork.
actual_capabilities: Creates a short design philosophy before visual production.
Directs output to Markdown, PNG, and PDF files.
Guides composition, color, space, typography, and minimal text use.
Uses bundled fonts from the ./canvas-fonts directory.
Supports single-page artwork and optional multi-page series.
Requires a second refinement pass for spacing and crisp execution.
limitations: It does not include a dedicated renderer or runnable generation script.
Output quality depends on the host agent and available design tooling.
Bundled font binaries need provenance review before marketplace publication.
It is not intended for editable UI mockups or production brand systems.

use_cases.title: Concept Poster Creation
use_cases.description: Turn an event, theme, or reference into a refined single-page visual artifact.

use_cases.title: Campaign Visual Exploration
use_cases.description: Generate expressive art directions before committing to a final marketing layout.

use_cases.title: Editorial Art Direction
use_cases.description: Create visual philosophies and image-led pages for essays, zines, or presentation covers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Poster
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one static artifact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a one-page PNG poster for a local night market. Use minimal text, strong composition, and a clear design philosophy.

prompt_templates.title: Turn a Theme Into Art
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with a conceptual reference.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PDF artwork about quiet climate anxiety. Make the reference subtle, visual, and sophisticated.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Visual Series
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multiple related pages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-page PNG series for a poetry launch. Each page should share one philosophy but feel distinct.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Editorial Piece
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request focused on polish and restraint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a museum-quality editorial cover for an essay on memory. Prioritize typography, margins, and final refinement.

output_examples.input: Create a poster for a small cinema night focused on silent films.
output_examples.output: A Markdown philosophy about muted motion, plus a PNG poster with sparse type, structured frames, and restrained contrast.

output_examples.input: Design a PDF artwork for a data privacy workshop.
output_examples.output: A single-page PDF using clinical grid marks, layered forms, and minimal labels to suggest privacy without long explanations.

output_examples.input: Make a three-page visual series for a modern poetry launch.
output: Page one establishes the visual philosophy through quiet type and broad negative space.
Page two introduces denser marks and warmer color tension.
Page three resolves the series with a restrained title and balanced composition.

best_practices: Provide the subject, desired format, and any required text before generation starts.
Ask for one page first when exploring a new visual direction.
Review font provenance and output boundaries before sharing final files.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for long explanatory copy inside the artwork.
Do not use this skill for exact imitation of living artists or protected brands.
Do not allow unapproved external font downloads in restricted environments.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a design philosophy and expresses it as PNG or PDF visual artwork.

faq.question: Does it create editable design files?
faq.answer: No. It targets static Markdown, PNG, and PDF outputs.

faq.question: Can it make multi-page work?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions include an option for related multi-page visual series.

faq.question: Does it include fonts?
faq.answer: Yes. It bundles many font files under ./canvas-fonts for local typography choices.

faq.question: Is it safe for automatic marketplace install?
faq.answer: Binary fonts and open-ended download instructions require review before automatic install.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
